title.en: Explain the meaning of an account, debit and credit
Apply the rules of debit and credit to the five types of accounts

say.en: Every account has two sides: debit on the left and credit on the right. A few simple rules tell us which side to use. In this lesson: Explain the meaning of an account, debit and credit.
Apply the rules of debit and credit to the five types of accounts.

body.en: An account is a summarised record of all transactions relating to one item, such as cash, a person or an expense. It is drawn in a T shape: the left side is the debit (Dr) side and the right side is the credit (Cr) side. *Debit and credit* do not mean good or bad; they only show the side on which an amount is written.
body.kn: ಖಾತೆ ಒಂದು ವಿಷಯಕ್ಕೆ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸಿದ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ವ್ಯವಹಾರಗಳ ಸಂಕ್ಷಿಪ್ತ ದಾಖಲೆ. ಎಡಭಾಗ ಡೆಬಿಟ್, ಬಲಭಾಗ ಕ್ರೆಡಿಟ್.

narration.en: Each transaction is recorded twice: one account is debited and another credited by the same amount, so assets always equal liabilities plus capital. Press the buttons and watch both sides move together. Buy goods on credit twice, then pay the creditor once. Which accounts changed? Can you make the beam tip? Why not?
narration.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ವ್ಯವಹಾರವನ್ನು ಎರಡು ಬಾರಿ ದಾಖಲಿಸಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ: ಒಂದು ಖಾತೆಗೆ ಡೆಬಿಟ್, ಇನ್ನೊಂದಕ್ಕೆ ಅದೇ ಮೊತ್ತದ ಕ್ರೆಡಿಟ್; ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಆಸ್ತಿ = ಹೊಣೆ + ಬಂಡವಾಳ. ಬಟನ್ ಒತ್ತಿ ಎರಡೂ ಬದಿ ಜೊತೆಗೆ ಬದಲಾಗುವುದನ್ನು ನೋಡಿ. ಎರಡು ಬಾರಿ ಸಾಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಖರೀದಿಸಿ, ಒಮ್ಮೆ ಸಾಲಗಾರನಿಗೆ ಪಾವತಿಸಿ. ಯಾವ ಖಾತೆಗಳು ಬದಲಾದವು? ತಕ್ಕಡಿಯನ್ನು ಓರೆ ಮಾಡಬಲ್ಲಿರಾ? ಏಕೆ ಆಗದು?

title.en: On the board: Rules of debit and credit

say.en: An account is drawn as a T. The left side is debit, the right side is credit.
Assets and expenses, including drawings and losses, increase on the debit side.
Liabilities, capital and revenues, including gains, increase on the credit side.
Apply the rule: what increases or decreases, and on which side?
Debit and credit are only sides, not good or bad.
On the board: Rules of debit and credit.

prompt.en: For each account, which side records an increase?
prompt.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಖಾತೆಗೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚಳವನ್ನು ಯಾವ ಬದಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ದಾಖಲಿಸಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ?

explanation.en: Assets, expenses, losses and drawings increase on the debit side. Liabilities, capital, revenues and gains increase on the credit side.

say.en: Debit or credit to increase? For each account, which side records an increase?

body.en: Under the accounting equation approach: assets and expenses (including losses and drawings) increase on the *debit* side and decrease on the credit side. Liabilities, capital and revenues (including gains) increase on the credit side and decrease on the debit side.
body.kn: ಆಸ್ತಿ ಮತ್ತು ವೆಚ್ಚ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾದರೆ ಡೆಬಿಟ್, ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾದರೆ ಕ್ರೆಡಿಟ್. ಹೊಣೆಗಾರಿಕೆ, ಬಂಡವಾಳ ಮತ್ತು ಆದಾಯ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾದರೆ ಕ್ರೆಡಿಟ್, ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾದರೆ ಡೆಬಿಟ್.

Under the accounting equation approach: assets and expenses (including losses and drawings) increase on the debit side and decrease on the credit side. Liabilities, capital and revenues including gains increase on the credit side and decrease on the debit side. Assets ↑ Dr, ↓ Cr.
say.kn: ಆಸ್ತಿ ಮತ್ತು ವೆಚ್ಚ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾದರೆ ಡೆಬಿಟ್, ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾದರೆ ಕ್ರೆಡಿಟ್. ಹೊಣೆಗಾರಿಕೆ, ಬಂಡವಾಳ ಮತ್ತು ಆದಾಯ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾದರೆ ಕ್ರೆಡಿಟ್, ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾದರೆ ಡೆಬಿಟ್.

say.en: Expenses and losses ↑ Dr.
Liabilities and capital ↑ Cr.
Revenues and gains ↑ Cr.

problem.en: State which account is debited and which is credited: (a) bought machinery for cash ₹50,000; (b) paid salary ₹12,000; (c) received interest ₹2,000; (d) took a bank loan ₹1,00,000.

answer.en: (a) Machinery Dr/Cash Cr (b) Salary Dr/Cash Cr (c) Cash Dr/Interest Cr (d) Cash Dr/Loan Cr

narration.en: Let us work this out step by step. State which account is debited and which is credited: (a) bought machinery for cash ₹50,000; (b) paid salary ₹12,000; (c) received interest ₹2,000; (d) took a bank loan ₹1,00,000.

say.en: Let us work this out step by step. State which account is debited and which is credited: a bought machinery for cash 50,000 rupees; b paid salary 12,000 rupees; c received interest 2,000 rupees; d took a bank loan 1,00,000 rupees.
a Machinery (asset ↑) Dr; Cash (asset ↓) Cr.
b Salary (expense ↑) Dr; Cash (asset ↓) Cr.
c Cash (asset ↑) Dr; Interest received (revenue ↑) Cr.
d Cash/Bank (asset ↑) Dr; Bank loan (liability ↑) Cr.
So the answer is a Machinery Dr over Cash Cr b Salary Dr over Cash Cr c Cash Dr over Interest Cr d Cash Dr over Loan Cr.
